workflowSummary: The tool continuously monitors your tracked contacts (customers and past champions) for job changes, and the moment one is detected, alerts the account owner with the person's new company and role — so a rep can re-engage a departed champion at their new company, or flag that an existing account just lost its internal advocate, instead of finding out months later when an email bounces.
samplePrompt: A champion at [Account] just left for [New Company]. Draft a short, warm reconnect message referencing what we worked on together, without being pushy about pitching anything yet.
beginnerNote: receiving and acting on a job-change alert is designed to be a quick, self-serve action for the account owner.
pricingNote: Plans typically price by number of tracked contacts, often in the low hundreds of dollars per month for smaller teams — verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article; job-change tracking should comply with applicable data-privacy rules for contact monitoring

title: I want a clear report showing a customer the actual return on investment they've gotten from us
workflowSummary: The tool pulls usage, outcome, and (where available) cost-savings or efficiency data tied to the account, and generates a plain-language progress report translating that into business impact — time saved, cost avoided, adoption growth — so an account manager has a concrete, data-backed story to bring into a renewal or expansion conversation instead of a vague 'things are going well.'
samplePrompt: Here's what changed for this account over the past year: [paste usage growth, efficiency metrics, or outcomes]. Turn this into a 3-bullet 'value delivered' summary I can put at the top of a customer-facing report.
beginnerNote: reading a generated value report is easy, but connecting the right usage/outcome data sources is a CS-ops setup task.
pricingNote: Mid-market CS platform pricing is typically quote-based — verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article; any customer-facing ROI figures should be validated against real account data before sharing externally

title: I want to track upsell and cross-sell revenue as its own pipeline, separate from new-business deals
workflowSummary: The tool tags and tracks expansion opportunities (upsells, cross-sells, seat additions) as a distinct pipeline from new-logo deals, rolling up expansion MRR/ARR separately in reporting — so leadership can see how much growth is coming from existing customers versus new ones, instead of both blending together in one generic pipeline number.
samplePrompt: Here's this month's pipeline broken into new-business and expansion deals [paste/describe]. Summarize in 3 sentences what share of pipeline is coming from existing customers versus new logos, and whether that mix looks healthy.
beginnerNote: separating and reporting on expansion pipeline is a RevOps/finance reporting task, not something an individual rep configures.
pricingNote: Billing/subscription analytics platforms like Maxio are typically quote-based for team plans — verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article; accurate expansion-vs-new-business splits depend on consistent deal-type tagging in the CRM

title: I want a single view of an account's overall health combining usage, support, and sentiment signals
workflowSummary: The tool pulls product usage trends, open/resolved support tickets, and sentiment from recent calls or surveys into a single account health score, updated continuously rather than reviewed once a quarter — so a CSM can spot a quietly declining account (usage down, tickets up, sentiment cooling) before it shows up as a churn or expansion problem later.
samplePrompt: Here's an account's recent signals: usage down 15% this month, 3 open support tickets, and their last call felt lukewarm [add detail]. In plain terms, how would you characterize this account's health, and what's the one thing to check first?
beginnerNote: checking a health score is a quick daily habit for a CSM, but setting up the combined scoring model is a CS-ops task.
pricingNote: Mid-market CS platform pricing is typically quote-based per managed account — verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article; health-score accuracy depends on the underlying usage, support, and sentiment data being connected and current

title: I want to run a customer advisory board with our most strategic accounts to guide our roadmap and messaging
workflowSummary: Invite your 12-20 most strategic customers into a structured program. The tool runs (or helps schedule) regular touchpoints — a live quarterly session plus shorter async check-ins — and captures what these customers say about your product, pricing, and roadmap, structuring their feedback into themes leadership can act on, instead of one unstructured meeting a quarter that produces a deck nobody revisits.
samplePrompt: Draft a short invitation email inviting a top customer to join our customer advisory board, explaining what it involves (roughly quarterly, ~1 hour, direct input into our roadmap) and why we specifically want their perspective.
beginnerNote: running a customer advisory board is a customer-marketing/leadership program, not something an individual account manager sets up alone.
pricingNote: Plans vary widely; some AI-interview-based tools price per interview (a few euros/dollars each), full community platforms are typically quote-based — verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article; participation should be voluntary and customers should be told clearly how their feedback will be used

title: I want customer success to flag an account to sales the moment it looks ready for expansion, without it falling through the cracks
workflowSummary: The tool scores every account for expansion propensity based on historical patterns (usage growth, engagement, similar accounts that expanded before), and automatically routes accounts crossing a threshold from the CSM's queue into the sales/AM team's pipeline with the relevant context attached — so an expansion-ready account gets a timely sales conversation instead of sitting in a CSM's book of business until the next scheduled check-in.
samplePrompt: This account just crossed our expansion-readiness threshold: [paste the signals, e.g. usage growth, upcoming renewal, recent positive feedback]. Draft a short handoff note from the CSM to the account manager summarizing why now is a good time to have the expansion conversation.
beginnerNote: expansion-readiness scoring and handoff routing is configured by CS-ops/RevOps; individual CSMs and AMs just receive the resulting handoff.
pricingNote: Mid-market CS platform pricing is typically quote-based — verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article; handoff routing thresholds should be reviewed periodically so accounts aren't handed off too early or too late

title: I want to build the case for a mid-contract price increase tied to an expansion, not at renewal time
workflowSummary: Pull together the account's usage growth and value-realization data alongside the proposed new pricing. The tool helps structure a business case that ties the price change to concrete value delivered or consumed (more seats, higher usage tier, new features adopted) rather than a flat increase with no justification, and routes it through the same approval workflow as other non-standard pricing changes.
samplePrompt: This account has grown usage by 40% since signing but is still on their original pricing tier. Draft a short, value-based justification for proposing a tier increase at their next check-in, framed around what they're getting rather than just the new price.
beginnerNote: proposing a mid-term price change is a deal-desk/account-management decision that typically needs manager or finance sign-off before it's raised with the customer.
pricingNote: Deal desk/CPQ platform pricing is typically quote-based for team licenses — verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article; any price change proposal should be reviewed against the existing contract terms before being raised with the customer

title: I want to report our net revenue retention and expansion metrics clearly to leadership
workflowSummary: Connect the tool to your billing/subscription data. It automatically calculates net revenue retention (expansion minus churn and contraction, as a percentage of starting revenue) and breaks the number down into its components, presenting it as a clean, board-ready chart — instead of finance manually reconciling billing exports in a spreadsheet each quarter to answer 'is our existing customer base growing or shrinking?'
samplePrompt: Our NRR this quarter came out to [X]%, made up of [Y]% expansion and [Z]% churn/contraction. Draft 2 sentences explaining what this number means for a board slide, in plain, non-jargon language.
beginnerNote: NRR reporting is a finance/RevOps function; individual sales reps don't typically configure or read this dashboard directly.
pricingNote: Subscription analytics tools often have plans starting around free-$100+/month depending on revenue scale — verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article; NRR calculations depend on clean, consistent billing data connected to the tool

title: I want to build a plan to grow our footprint inside an account where a competitor is also being used
workflowSummary: The tool flags when a competitor is mentioned in customer calls or support conversations tied to an account, and surfaces the relevant competitive battlecard content (differentiators, objection responses) so the account team can build a specific plan to expand into the parts of the account still served by the competitor, instead of reacting one conversation at a time without a coordinated strategy.
samplePrompt: This account uses us for [use case] but still uses [Competitor] for [other use case]. Draft a short internal talking-points list for why we could take over that second use case too, based on our known differentiators.
beginnerNote: reading a competitor-mention alert is easy, but building the full displacement strategy is an account-manager/sales-leadership task.
pricingNote: Bundled into conversation-intelligence and competitive-intelligence platform pricing, typically quote-based per seat — verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article; competitive displacement plans should be reviewed against the specific contract terms already in place with the account

title: I want to benchmark a customer's usage against similar customers to make the case for an upgrade
workflowSummary: The tool compares one account's product usage and adoption against a peer group of similar customers (by size, industry, or plan tier), highlighting where the account is behind or ahead of typical usage for their segment — giving an account manager a data point like 'similar customers your size use X feature 3x more often' to make an upgrade conversation concrete instead of a vague 'you should use more of the product.'
samplePrompt: This customer's usage of [feature] is roughly half of what similar-sized customers in [industry] typically show. Draft 2 sentences I could say on a call to introduce this comparison without sounding like I'm pressuring them.
beginnerNote: reading a benchmark comparison is easy for an account manager, but building the peer-group benchmarking model is a product-analytics/CS-ops task.
pricingNote: Product analytics platform pricing varies; Pendo has a free tier for small teams, enterprise tiers are quote-based — verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article; peer benchmarking depends on having enough comparable accounts in the same segment to make a meaningful comparison
